summary: Generated single-id DELETE commands for syncable resources (acl-rules, dns policies, firewall policies/zones, hotspot vouchers, networks, traffic-matching-lists, wifi broadcasts) never removed the corresponding row from the local SQLite mirror after a successful live delete. Added internal/cli/mirror_cleanup.go (hand-authored, preserved by regen-merge) and internal/store/store.go:DeleteResource, wired into each affected generated *_delete.go command.
reason: Without this, drift/search/rule-predict/topology kept showing a deleted resource as still present until the next full sync, which for a config-drift-detection CLI is a materially wrong local answer, not just staleness. Found by Greptile review on the publish PR (library/devices/unifi/internal/cli/sites_networks_delete.go), confirmed to repeat identically across the other 7 single-id delete commands on syncable resources. The bulk-filtered hotspot delete-vouchers endpoint was deliberately left unfixed: the API's filter is opaque server-side and does not report which voucher ids were removed, so wiping the entire local mirror for that site would trade one wrong-answer shape for another (falsely showing vouchers as gone that the filter didn't actually match).
validated_outcome: Live-verified against the real gateway: created a disposable traffic-matching-list, synced it into the local mirror, deleted it via 'unifi-pp-cli sites traffic-matching-lists delete', and confirmed the generic resources row, the typed traffic_matching_lists row, and the FTS index entry were all removed, matching the live API's own confirmation that the resource no longer exists.
